# Expert Review Brief — Accelerator Bandwidth Comparability (IDE-012)

This brief invites specialists in semiconductor memory and accelerator interconnects to review one bounded question each, using public material only. It accompanies the research dossier `ACCELERATOR_BANDWIDTH_COMPARABILITY_DOSSIER_012.md`, which is an AI-assisted research candidate and has not been reviewed by any person.

## Terms

- Participation is voluntary and unpaid. There is no deadline and no obligation to answer every question.
- You may review a single question. Disagreement, criticism and "this cannot be settled from public material" are all useful answers.
- Use only public, non-confidential material. Please do not share anything under NDA or not yet published.
- You will be named only if you give explicit permission, and only in the form you approve. Otherwise your contribution is recorded without attribution.
- A response is recorded as a specialist's comment on the question it answers. It is not represented as validation of the dossier, and AI-assisted analysis in the dossier is never presented as independent human review.

## Questions

### 1. In AMD's MI300X documentation, does 'P2P ring peak aggregate' bandwidth (896 GB/s) describe one GPU's seven links or a platform-level quantity?

- **Why it matters:** It decides whether the figure can sit beside any per-GPU fabric figure.
- **What would settle it:** An AMD statement of the figure's scope, or a version-identified copy of the 2025 CDNA 4 edition with endnote MI350-007
- **Public materials:** Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., “AMD Instinct MI300X Platform (data sheet)” (2023-12-04), https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/instinct-tech-docs/data-sheets/amd-instinct-mi300x-platform-data-sheet.pdf; Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., “AMD Instinct MI300X Accelerator (data sheet)” (2025-06-16), https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/instinct-tech-docs/data-sheets/amd-instinct-mi300x-data-sheet.pdf; Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., “Introducing AMD CDNA 3 Architecture (white paper)” (2025-04-07), https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/instinct-tech-docs/white-papers/amd-cdna-3-white-paper.pdf
- **Dossier section:** case `case-a-mi300x`.

### 2. Do NVIDIA's 22 TB/s and 19.2 TB/s per-GPU memory figures describe different Rubin configurations, and if so which?

- **Why it matters:** Every per-GPU Rubin memory comparison depends on which figure applies to which product.
- **What would settle it:** An NVIDIA specification that ties each figure to a configuration or memory operating point
- **Public materials:** NVIDIA, “NVIDIA HGX Platform” (2026-09-30), https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/hgx/; NVIDIA, “NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72” (2026-10-21), https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/vera-rubin-nvl72/; NVIDIA Corporation, “Inside NVIDIA Rubin GPU Architecture: Powering the Era of Agentic AI” (2026-07-21), https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/inside-nvidia-rubin-gpu-architecture-powering-the-era-of-agentic-ai/; NVIDIA Corporation, “Five Ways NVIDIA Co-Design Maximizes the Value of Every Byte in the AI Factory” (2026-11-05), https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/five-ways-nvidia-co-design-maximizes-the-value-of-every-byte-in-the-ai-factory
- **Dossier section:** case `case-b-rubin-memory`.

### 3. What counting convention gives 3.6 TB/s and what gives 3 TB/s per Rubin GPU for NVLink 6, given that NVIDIA's system aggregates divide evenly to 3 TB/s?

- **Why it matters:** Scale-up comparisons and rack-to-GPU conversions depend on one consistent convention.
- **What would settle it:** An NVIDIA statement of direction and counting for both figures
- **Public materials:** NVIDIA Corporation, “Inside the NVIDIA Vera Rubin Platform: Six New Chips, One AI Supercomputer” (2026-01-05), https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/inside-the-nvidia-rubin-platform-six-new-chips-one-ai-supercomputer/; NVIDIA, “NVIDIA HGX Platform” (2026-09-30), https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/hgx/; NVIDIA, “NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72” (2026-10-21), https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/vera-rubin-nvl72/
- **Dossier section:** case `case-c-nvlink6`.

### 4. For the x16 PCIe Gen 6 and CXL 3.0 figures of 256 GB/s, what share remains after encoding, FEC and protocol overhead?

- **Why it matters:** Raw link figures are often compared with delivered throughput; the overhead decides how far they differ.
- **What would settle it:** The normative PCIe 6.0 and CXL 3.x specifications, or a published measurement with its method
- **Public materials:** CXL Consortium, “Compute Express Link 3.0 (white paper)” (2022-08-02), https://computeexpresslink.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/CXL_3.0_white-paper_FINAL.pdf; NVIDIA Corporation, “Inside NVIDIA Rubin GPU Architecture: Powering the Era of Agentic AI” (2026-07-21), https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/inside-nvidia-rubin-gpu-architecture-powering-the-era-of-agentic-ai/

### 5. Which published, reproducible measurements of collective bandwidth exist for the MI300X eight-GPU platform or Vera Rubin NVL72, and with what methods?

- **Why it matters:** No figure in the dossier is measured; measured throughput is the evidence most comparisons actually need.
- **What would settle it:** A measurement with workload, message sizes, software versions and topology stated
- **Public materials:** none identified; pointing to any would itself help.
